subject: Post-call: SLO gating, test windows and customer-driven stress ops plan
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@astersoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: SLO gating, test windows and customer-driven stress ops plan

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the dry run: 

1) SLO targets you called out (please confirm):
   - p95 latency for sync generation calls < 300ms (50–512 tokens)
   - p99 < 800ms for spikes
   - Sustained throughput target: 50 req/s for the main API path, with bursts up to 200 req/s for short windows
   - Streaming concurrency: support 150 concurrent streaming connections with per-connection tail latency < 150ms

2) Test mechanics you requested:
   - Customer-led execution using k6 (you mentioned you also have a Locust variant)
   - Redwood to provide a dedicated test account + API key and a short canary ramp plan
   - IP allowlist: you will provide a public CIDR set we must add to your allowlist; Redwood will share our egress ranges too

3) Proposed schedule:
   - Dry run (non-peak): Friday June 4, 10:00–12:00 PT (Redwood + AsterSoft validation)
   - Full customer-led window: June 7–9, 09:00–17:00 PT (rolling ramp each day)

Attachments: I asked Sarah to send the k6 profile and any IP ranges so we can pre-seed the allowlist.

Next actions: 
   - Sarah: confirm the SLO numbers above and share the k6 script + IP list (if you prefer Locust, include that script too).
   - Marissa/Karthik: prep a dedicated test account with a scoped API key, enable request-logging at token-level for the window, and draft a canary ramp (5m -> 1m -> 30s steps) for the dry run.

If we get the artifacts today we can validate credentials and do a quick smoke test before Friday.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@astersoft.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@astersoft.com>, ops@astersoft.com
Date: 2027-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO gating, test windows and customer-driven stress ops plan

Thanks Diego — confirming the numbers below and attaching our baseline k6 profile and our egress ranges. Small clarifications: 

- p95 < 300ms is our target for the production inference endpoint used by user-facing flows; we want Redwood to validate the same path (including auth and any pre/post-processing hooks).
- For streaming: we expect 150 concurrent readers on the websocket endpoint; we care most about tail delivery for the last-token latency.
- Throughput: 50 sustained req/s is the long-run SLA we’re designing for; during event spikes we will generate up to 200 req/s for ~10–15 minutes.

We will run the k6 test (attached: AsterSoft_k6_profile.yml) and can also provide a Locust script if needed. Attaching ip_ranges.csv with our corporate NATs. Evan will coordinate the test ops side on our end.

Preferred windows: June 7–9 for the full run. We can do a quick dry run Friday (June 4) 10–12 PT. Please share Redwood IP egress ranges to add to our allowlist.

Attachments: AsterSoft_k6_profile.yml (script), ip_ranges.csv (customer NAT ranges)

— Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Platform Reliability, AsterSoft
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: SLO gating, test windows and customer-driven stress ops plan

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Sarah’s confirmation and artifacts. Action items for Redwood ops and QA: 

- Create dedicated test tenant: scope to inference-only, limit tokens to 500k/day, generate API key labeled AW-TEST-0610.
- Enable per-request tracing and token-level cost logging for the test key; we’ll need that to correlate latency vs token lengths.
- Load test plan (attach draft runbook): include a canary sequence for the dry run (10 req/s -> 30 -> 60 -> 120 -> 200, 10m holds at each steady state) and a communications play (Slack channel + paging list).
- Validate the k6 profile attached by AsterSoft; request a Locust variant if our streaming harness needs it.

Marissa: can your on-call perf engineer review the k6 waves and confirm whether we need any model variant (smaller quantized profile) for the initial ramp?
Karthik: can infra pre-authorize the AW public CIDRs (from ip_ranges.csv) to the temp allowlist and confirm Redwood’s egress ranges for Sarah?

I’m tagging the runbook_draft.md to start capturing test steps. If we can validate creds and do a quick smoke today, we’ll be in good shape for Friday.

— Diego
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: SLO gating, test windows and customer-driven stress ops plan

Thanks — reviewed Sarah’s profile. Quick notes from perf: 

- We should capture the following metrics during every wave: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate (4xx/5xx), token-per-request distribution, connection churn for streaming, and server-side CPU/GPU utilization.
- For the dry run I recommend a conservative canary: 5m at 10 req/s, 10m at 30 req/s, 15m at 60 req/s. If everything is green move to 120 then 200 for 10m each.
- Model variant: start with the production model they want to use. If we see sustained GPU saturation (>70%) we’ll switch to a quantized variant for the burst windows and document the delta.

Karthik — please confirm the allowlist flow: we need to add AsterSoft CIDRs to the customer allowlist in console (they asked us to pre-seed) and also produce a 5–6 IP egress range set for them to allow inbound from Redwood. I’ll draft the communications templates (Slack + Ops-runbook).

I’ll attach an initial SLO-matrix.xlsx to the runbook with gating rules (green/yellow/red thresholds) and the rollback criteria.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Performance Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@astersoft.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@astersoft.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO gating, test windows and customer-driven stress ops plan

Thanks Marissa — that looks good. Evan and I talked and we’ll: 

- Add the Redwood egress list to our allowlist once you send it (please include both IPv4 CIDRs and specific ephemeral ports if applicable).
- We'll run the dry run Friday (June 4) 10:00–12:00 PT; Evan will lead the k6 execution and share a live Grafana link.
- For the full run (June 7–9) we will coordinate daily rollups and a 30-minute postmortem each evening.

I’ll upload the Locust script this afternoon in case you want to test streaming concurrency from our side. If you can provision the test key today we’ll do a quick smoke tonight.

On Fri we’ll start with the conservative canary Marissa suggested and notify you on Slack before each ramp step.

Best — Sarah
